matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and compute the difference between the two sides of the equation; this guides which value changes are needed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any matchstick equation, before considering stick moves.
matchstick.example: Attempting to move a stick without first calculating that the left side (12) and right side (17) differ by 5.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be relocated from any character to any other character, respecting the shape constraints of Roman numerals and operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate the full set of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Considering only moving sticks from operators, ignoring possible moves from numerals like X.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the numeric values of the affected numerals change and check whether the net change equals the previously computed discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' but not accounting for the resulting numeric change of 38.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the '=' sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of them can turn it into a '-' while the remaining stick stays a valid minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy suggests reducing or increasing the total by a small amount that can be achieved by changing the equality operator.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=', turning it into '-', but forgetting to adjust the rest of the equation accordingly.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick turns it into a '-' (horizontal only).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a sign change from addition to subtraction could resolve the numeric discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to another character, turning '+' into '-', but leaving the vertical stick destination invalid.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be transferred directly from one operator to another, simultaneously altering both operators (e.g., moving a horizontal from '=' to '+' to make '+' an '=', and '=' a '-').
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy can be fixed by changing two operators with a single stick move.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '+' to '=', creating an invalid operator shape.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral would increase its value by the needed amount, consider moving a stick from an operator to that numeral, ensuring both source and destination remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required numeric change matches a known operator‑to‑numeral transformation.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '+' to a numeral, resulting in an invalid numeral shape.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', and each side must have at least one numeral and valid operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: As a final validation step before outputting the answer.
matchstick.example: Removing the only '=' sign, leaving the equation without an equality.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Map common single‑stick changes (X↔V, I↔V, I↔X) to their numeric value changes (±5, ±4, ±9) and use this mapping to directly match the required discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy is small (≤9) and a direct numeral transformation could resolve it.
matchstick.example: Missing the X→V transformation that reduces the value by 5, and instead trying unrelated operator changes.

matchstick.title: Identical numerals operator conversion
matchstick.principle: If both sides already contain the same numeral, moving a stick from the '+' operator to turn it into an '=', creating a second equality, yields a trivially true equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the left‑hand side numeral equals the right‑hand side numeral(s) before any move.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' without noticing that converting '+' to '=' would make the equation trivially true.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick without checking that the source or destination character still conforms to a valid Roman numeral or operator shape.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, verify that both the source and destination characters are still valid (or eliminated only if they are a single‑stick numeral).

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the stick move but does not recompute the arithmetic result to ensure the equation balances.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate the whole equation numerically after applying a candidate move before committing to the answer.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the process of moving sticks, the model may accidentally delete a character or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat the equation as a fixed sequence of tokens; only relocate sticks, never delete characters unless the character is a single‑stick numeral being eliminated intentionally.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Changing '+' to '-' (or similar) alters the arithmetic dramatically, but the model does not account for that change in its discrepancy calculation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator is altered, recompute the numeric effect of the sign change and include it in the discrepancy matching step.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes adds or removes sticks instead of moving exactly one.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce the invariant that exactly one stick is taken from a source character and placed onto a destination character; no sticks may be created or destroyed.
